name: claude-code

detect.version_re_notes: `claude --version` prints e.g. "2.1.260 (Claude Code)" (live 2026-09-10). The npm global install puts only script shims on PATH; claude.cmd execs %dp0%\node_modules\@anthropic-ai\claude-code\bin\claude.exe directly (read 2026-09-10), so npm_exe resolves the REAL native binary under the shim's node_modules without a shell. (There is no package-level cli.js; the shim does not route through one.)

command.mode_args_notes: Only workspace-write (acceptEdits) and unattended (bypassPermissions) are callable. permission-prompts=none is common to all print calls: it denies operations that still need approval, but does not revoke existing native allow rules for Write/Edit/Bash/MCP tools. The previous default+none read-only recipe was disproved by an allow:Write counterexample; read-only is unsupported and has no invocation mapping.
command.argv_notes: stream-json REQUIRES --verbose in print mode (cli-reference). Live stream shape sampled 2026-09-10 on v2.1.260: NDJSON on stdout = system/init event -> assistant events -> one terminal result event. Native 2.1.270 re-verified 2026-09-18: selected full model ID with native --effort low passed file-write and cross-process resume probes; read-only was refused before dispatch. User settings.json bytes stayed unchanged. Other permissions were not re-probed.

env._env_notes: native_default = paidan does not set the variable at all (claude runs against the user's real ~/.claude, incl. the ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN/ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL gateway entry in native settings.json env). Paidan never stages or copies claude config.

fs.read.via: built-in read-only tools (Read/Glob/Grep) are auto-allowed in every permission mode; static deny rules still apply on top

fs.write.via: acceptEdits auto-accepts Edit/Write; bypassPermissions is used for unattended. Native allow rules can authorize writes even in default mode with permission-prompts=none; there is no enforced read-only preset.

shell.exec.via: Bash is available under bypassPermissions or existing native allow rules. With acceptEdits/default, operations still needing approval are denied by permission-prompts=none. This does not revoke already authorized commands.

net.fetch.via: WebFetch/WebSearch appear in the init event tool list (live sample 2026-09-10); per-mode auto-allow behavior in print mode not probed

interact.ask.via: print mode has no user-answer channel; --permission-prompts none turns every prompt into a denial (P2 2026-09-09). --permission-prompt-tool exists but needs an MCP prompt tool paidan does not provide

permission.presets_notes: workspace-write maps to acceptEdits; unattended maps to bypassPermissions. All print invocations use permission-prompts=none. Native allow rules still authorize tools without asking, so default+none does not enforce read-only; paidan rejects read-only rather than modifying user settings. Approval suppression and allowed capabilities are separate.

denial_evidence.via: stream-json terminal result event carries permission_denials[] ({tool_name, tool_use_id, tool_input}); the claude-stream-json parser surfaces them into result.json evidence notes (P2 live 2026-09-09: Write denial visible, exit 0, subtype success)

permission.headless_notes: Print mode defaults to acceptEdits with permission-prompts=none. Requests needing approval are denied, not routed to an absent SDK host. Broader bypassPermissions requires an explicitly selected unattended mode. Existing native allow rules remain effective; read-only is unsupported.

resume.notes: Session handle = session_id of the stream-json system/init event (a UUID; stable across resume — P3 2026-09-09 recalled P1 content with the same id). Official constraints (code.claude.com/docs/en, 2026-09-09): (1) `-p --resume` tiers by the NEW -p invocation (back to default/Manual) — nothing is inherited from the original run, so startup flags (--permission-mode/--model/--add-dir/--settings/--mcp-config) MUST be re-passed; paidan always re-splices mode_args/model_arg on resume, which satisfies this. (2) Two processes must NOT resume the same session concurrently — both would interleave writes into one transcript (officially warned; treated as forbidden). (3) --resume searches projects machine-wide (2.1.223+), so a same-cwd resume run resolves the session. Model on resume: inherited from transcript unless --model overrides.

models.notes: Static aliases plus current configured full IDs, alias mappings and custom selector; known model effort metadata, not an account-access guarantee. Fixed defaults bind to the user-approved selection_context; native home routing/model/effort changes require user selection again. Project/managed layers and server restrictions are not fully resolved. Credentials remain native.

parser_notes: stdout NDJSON (stream-json): system/init carries session_id; assistant events carry message.content[] text parts; the single terminal result event carries result text, session_id (cross-checked against init), usage (input/output/cache tokens), total_cost_usd and permission_denials. Non-JSON lines / mid-line EOF / conflicting session ids degrade the parser (terminal judgment then cannot be exit-code-based).

capabilities._capabilities_notes: --bg exists but is mutually exclusive with -p, so no native background for print-mode runs.

effort.notes: Uses the native --effort flag only; omitted effort follows native defaults. Native environment/settings overrides and model/organization limits remain authoritative. paidan does not inject --settings to override a user's forced effort. Options are adapter syntax, not every model's capability.
